subject.title: Gateway memory growth due to repeated file read errors

question: Should the remaining fix target the scheduled producer/prompt that asks for invalid paths, or should the read tool contract change to tolerate directory paths and inferred memory paths?
rationale: Source proves partial fixes and a remaining directory failure shape, but the correct owner boundary depends on whether maintainers want producer-specific correction or broader read-tool behavior.

options.title: Fix the producer after live repro
options.body: Reproduce the scheduled Gateway path on current main and patch the code that emits memory-system/CORE.md or memory/agent-tasks file reads.

options.title: Accept scoped memory fallback only
options.body: Review the existing daily-memory fallback PR as a partial fix while leaving CORE.md, directory reads, and RSS growth open for separate proof.

options.title: Broaden read-tool semantics
options.body: Intentionally change read to list directories or infer memory paths, with explicit tests and compatibility review for model-facing tool behavior.

recommendation.title: Fix the producer after live repro
recommendation.body: Reproduce the scheduled Gateway path on current main and patch the code that emits memory-system/CORE.md or memory/agent-tasks file reads.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history touches both read-tool and heartbeat scheduling boundaries, making this a practical owner for the producer-versus-tool contract decision.
